Jupiter has ninety-five moons, including Callisto and Adrastea.
Callisto completes an orbit of Jupiter in 16.69 Earth days on average. Adrastea completes an orbit of Jupiter in 0.30 Earth days on average. German mathematician and astronomer Johannes Kepler (1571–1630) described the orbits of planets as elliptical in shape rather than circular. Kepler published three laws of planetary motion to describe the orbits of planets around the Sun. Kepler’s laws also apply to the elliptical orbits of natural satellites (e.g., moons).
questions.prompt: The student wants to contrast the orbits of the two moons. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Adrastea completes its orbit of Jupiter many times faster than Callisto does.
choices.B: Jupiter’s moons, specifically Callisto and Adrastea, orbit their planet in the same way the planets orbit the Sun.
choices.C: Kepler’s three laws of planetary motion describe the orbits of planets and natural satellites, including those of Callisto and Adrastea.
choices.D: Callisto’s orbit of Jupiter is elliptical in shape and takes, on average, 16.69 Earth days, while Adrastea’s orbit of Jupiter is circular in shape and takes, on average, 0.30 Earth days.
